name: Defense Intelligence Agency

summary.text: The Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) is the Pentagon's principal military intelligence agency. On this site it appears twice: as the contracting agency for the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP), awarded in September 2008 to Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies after a 2008 supplemental appropriation tasked DIA with studying foreign advanced aerospace weapon threats, and as the author of a preliminary assessment, reported in June 2025, that U.S. strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities had set the programme back by months. DIA's FOIA reading room holds the AAWSAP contract briefings, statement of work and an internal memo on Senator Harry Reid's 2009 request to place the programme under special access protection.

facts.claim: A 2009 DIA status briefing released under FOIA states that a July 2008 supplemental appropriation tasked DIA to study foreign advanced aerospace weapon threats from the present out to 40 years in the future, with $10 million in initial FY2008 funds, and that in September 2008 DIA awarded the AAWSAP contract to the sole bidder, Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies of Las Vegas.

facts.claim: An internal DIA memo released under FOIA addresses Senator Harry Reid's 2009 request to place the AAWSAP programme under Special Access Program protection; DIA's review found no justification and the memo recommended against establishing a Special Access Program.

facts.claim: A 2009 DIA briefing identifies the AAWSAP contract as HHM402-08-C-0072 with Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies LLC as contractor and a start date of 21 September 2008; the public solicitation and statement of work were dated August 2008. The Black Vault, which obtained the records through FOIA requests filed in 2018, reports that DIA released additional records on October 13, 2022 with 13 pages withheld in full.

facts.claim: The Debrief reported the AAWSAP contract was worth about $22 million, and quoted Senator Reid as saying Bigelow was not pre-selected; the DIA briefing describes Bigelow as the sole bidder.

facts.claim: In June 2025 CNN and Reuters reported, citing unnamed sources, that a preliminary assessment prepared by the Defense Intelligence Agency concluded the U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities had delayed Tehran's programme by only a matter of months, with one source estimating the earliest restart in one to two months. The White House called the reported conclusion flat-out wrong, and administration officials later described the assessment as low-confidence and overtaken by later intelligence.
facts.quote: The initial report was prepared by the Defense Intelligence Agency, the Pentagon's main intelligence arm and one of 18 U.S. intelligence agencies, said two of the sources.

facts.claim: On March 25, 2025 Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard told the Senate Intelligence Committee that the intelligence community continued to assess that Iran was not building a nuclear weapon and that Supreme Leader Khamenei had not authorized the programme suspended in 2003, while noting Iran's enriched uranium stockpile was at its highest level. After the June 2025 strikes President Trump said he did not care what she had said.
facts.quote: continues to assess that Iran is not building a nuclear weapon

openQuestions: Site claim (Demystification): '$22 million in public defense funds' for AAWSAP is reported by The Debrief and, per the existing bigelow-aerospace file, confirmed by the Pentagon in December 2017; the DIA briefing itself cites $10 million in initial FY2008 funds, and the full contract value was not found in a DIA document.

Site claim (Demystification): that AAWSAP funds 'directly financed paranormal pseudoscientific investigations into Bigelow's privately owned real estate (Skinwalker Ranch)' is not supported by the DIA solicitation, which The Black Vault notes contains nothing matching paranormal study; the DIA memo describes the purpose as investigating future aerospace technologies. Unsupported on the records opened.

Site claim (Demystification): 'sole-source contract' conflicts with DIA's description of a public solicitation won by the sole bidder, and with Senator Reid's statement that Bigelow was not pre-selected.

Site claim (Recurring Cast): 'the Defense Intelligence Agency's initial assessment, as reported, said the programme was set back months' is supported by Reuters/CNN reporting; the assessment itself has not been published.
The DIA memo at FileId/237660 is said to describe AAWSAP as officially the contract that Senator Reid's letter called AATIP; this was not read directly and should be checked.
Contract identifiers differ between documents (HHM402-08-R-0211 in the FOIA request, HHM402-08-C-0072 in the 2009 briefing); the former appears to be the solicitation number.
